words.sense: A predictable, obvious moral pronouncement offered as if it provides meaningful comfort or advice.
misconceptions: Every overused phrase is life advice.

words.sense: An expression or idea made unoriginal by repeated use, regardless of purpose.
misconceptions: Advice sounds insightful merely because it is positive.

semantic_axes.description: A platitude is a worn, obvious life lesson presented as wisdom; a cliché is any stale expression or idea, even without moral advice.

edges.boundary_rule: A platitude is a worn, obvious life lesson presented as wisdom; a cliché is any stale expression or idea, even without moral advice.

misconceptions.M1: Every overused phrase is life advice.
misconceptions.M2: Advice sounds insightful merely because it is positive.
misconceptions.M3: An overused narrative device must be a moral statement.

chains.frame: Which noun best describes the advice Nisha gave her friend?

beats.text: When her friend feared failing, Nisha offered, “Just believe in yourself, and everything will work out.”
beats.decisive_clue: empty reassurance offered as useful wisdom
beats.reason: The sweeping advice does not engage with the actual exam problem.

beats.text: She printed the sentence on a colorful card for the friend’s desk.
beats.decisive_clue: generic comfort offered as wisdom despite decorative card
beats.reason: Presentation does not supply practical insight.

chains.feedback_short: The broad reassurance offers no useful guidance; a colorful card does not change that.
chains.feedback_deep: A platitude is a commonplace moral or comforting claim offered as though it contains insight. A cliché is any overused expression, not necessarily advice.
chains.contrast_rule: A platitude poses as wisdom; a cliché has simply been used too often.

hints.attention: Ask what kind of help the words actually offer.
hints.axis: A platitude is a worn, obvious life lesson presented as wisdom; a cliché is any stale expression or idea, even without moral advice.
hints.contrast: A platitude poses as wisdom; a cliché has simply been used too often.

chains.frame: Which noun best describes the phrase in Luca’s story?

beats.text: Luca ended the mystery with, “And then it was all just a dream.”
beats.reason: The twist is familiar through countless stories, not a moral lesson.

beats.text: He added a final line about waking up relieved, but the same ending still erased the entire plot.
beats.decisive_clue: the worn dream-ending device still drives the conclusion
beats.reason: Extra wording does not make the overused twist original.

chains.feedback_short: The familiar dream ending remains a worn story device, not advice or moral insight.
chains.feedback_deep: Clichés include overused ideas, plots, and phrases. Platitudes are specifically stale statements offered as meaningful wisdom or comfort.
chains.contrast_rule: A platitude poses as wisdom; a cliché has simply been used too often.

hints.attention: Decide whether the problem is an overused plot or a life lesson.
hints.axis: A platitude is a worn, obvious life lesson presented as wisdom; a cliché is any stale expression or idea, even without moral advice.
hints.contrast: A platitude poses as wisdom; a cliché has simply been used too often.

chains.frame: Which noun best describes Farid’s response to a breakup?

beats.text: Farid told his upset sister, “Time heals all wounds,” then offered no further response to what had happened.
beats.decisive_clue: standard comfort presented in place of specific support
beats.reason: The sentence is a broad consoling maxim offered as if it addresses her situation.

beats.text: After hearing the sentence in a film earlier that morning, Farid repeated the same line to his sister as comfort.
beats.decisive_clue: the familiar line is still being used as empty consolation
beats.reason: Its source explains why it is familiar, but Farid’s use of it as generic comfort makes platitude the more precise choice.

chains.feedback_short: The film explains the line’s familiarity, but Farid still uses it as all-purpose comfort.
chains.feedback_deep: A platitude is a banal maxim offered as meaningful comfort or advice. The line may also be a cliché because it is familiar, but its consoling function makes platitude more precise.
chains.contrast_rule: A platitude is stale wisdom or comfort; a cliché is any expression or idea made unoriginal by repetition.

hints.attention: Focus on why Farid repeats the line to his sister.
hints.axis: A platitude is a worn, obvious life lesson presented as wisdom; a cliché is any stale expression or idea, even without moral advice.
hints.contrast: A platitude is stale wisdom or comfort; a cliché is any expression or idea made unoriginal by repetition.

chains.frame: Which noun best describes the phrase in Ana’s travel advertisement?

beats.text: Ana titled every holiday package “a hidden gem” despite using the same wording as dozens of competing ads.
beats.decisive_clue: a stock promotional expression repeated everywhere
beats.reason: The tired phrase offers no moral guidance.

beats.text: She used it for beaches, cities, and mountain hotels alike.
beats.decisive_clue: the stock label is reused regardless of destination
beats.reason: Its indiscriminate repetition makes it even less original.

chains.feedback_short: “A hidden gem” is worn promotional wording, not a piece of moral advice.
chains.feedback_deep: Clichés are familiar phrases or ideas weakened by overuse. Platitudes involve obvious moral truths presented as wisdom or reassurance.
chains.contrast_rule: A platitude poses as wisdom; a cliché has simply been used too often.

hints.attention: Is the expression selling something or offering a life lesson?
hints.axis: A platitude is a worn, obvious life lesson presented as wisdom; a cliché is any stale expression or idea, even without moral advice.
hints.contrast: A platitude poses as wisdom; a cliché has simply been used too often.

chains.frame: Which noun best describes the ending of Mei’s film script?

beats.text: Mei’s two rivals confessed their feelings and kissed in the rain as a dramatic song started.
beats.decisive_clue: stock romantic ending used in countless stories
beats.reason: This is a familiar narrative device rather than advice.

beats.text: She added an umbrella blowing away just before the kiss.
beats.decisive_clue: the worn romantic scene remains despite a small prop change
beats.reason: A minor variation does not remove the familiar storytelling pattern.

chains.feedback_short: The rain-soaked confession is a stock romantic scene even with an extra umbrella.
chains.feedback_deep: Cliché is broad enough for repeated plot moments and imagery. Platitude specifically concerns tired moral or consoling statements given as wisdom.
chains.contrast_rule: A platitude poses as wisdom; a cliché has simply been used too often.
